sn44.10:1.1: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One … and said to him:
sn44.10:1.3: “How is it now, Master Gotama, is there a self?”
sn44.10:1.4: When this was said, the Blessed One was silent.
sn44.10:1.5: “Then, Master Gotama, is there no self?”
sn44.10:1.6: A second time the Blessed One was silent.
sn44.10:1.7: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and departed.
sn44.10:2.1: Then, not long after the wanderer Vacchagotta had left, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One:
sn44.10:2.2: “Why is it, venerable sir, that when the Blessed One was questioned by the wanderer Vacchagotta, he did not answer?”
sn44.10:2.3: “If, Ānanda, when I was asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there a self?’ I had answered, ‘There is a self,’ this would have been siding with those ascetics and brahmins who are eternalists.
sn44.10:2.4: And if, when I was asked by him, ‘Is there no self?’ I had answered, ‘There is no self,’ this would have been siding with those ascetics and brahmins who are annihilationists.
sn44.10:2.5: “If, Ānanda, when I was asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there a self?’ I had answered, ‘There is a self,’ would this have been consistent on my part with the arising of the knowledge that
sn44.10:2.8: “And if, when I was asked by him, ‘Is there no self?’ I had answered, ‘There is no self,’ the wanderer Vacchagotta, already confused, would have fallen into even greater confusion, thinking,
sn44.10:2.9: ‘It seems that the self I formerly had does not exist now.’”
